# Preface {.unnumbered}

This report describes snapy as the code implements it: for each scheme, what it does, where it comes from, how
it is discretized, where it lives in the code, how it is tested and where it stops working. Every statement is
derived on the page, cited to the code at a pinned commit, or cited to a test with its tolerance.

## How the book is organized {#sec-preface-map .unnumbered}

The chapters follow one stage of the model from the equations outward, at the code pin below. Each chapter
section has the same layers: a summary, the derivation, the numerical method, the code, the tests and the limits.

| chapter | what it covers |
|---|---|
| @sec-ch01 | The step at a glance: how a deck becomes a block and its modules, the driver loop, the stage, and a map of the source tree |
| @sec-ch02 | The conservation laws and the state vectors, and the equations of state that convert between conserved and primitive variables: ideal gas, ideal moist mixture, the temperature-dependent moist mixture, the tabulated and shallow-water closures, and the phase equilibrium |
| @sec-ch03 | The grids: Cartesian, spherical-polar and the gnomonic cubed sphere, their metric quantities, the split into blocks, what a ghost cell holds at each kind of face, and the cubed-sphere panel seams |
| @sec-ch04 | The semi-discrete operator of a stage: the $x_1$ conversion between cell averages and point values, reconstruction to faces, the Riemann solvers, the face-flux covariance terms, the flux divergence and the geometric sources |
| @sec-ch05 | How the $x_1$ sweep keeps a stratified column at rest: the hydrostatic reference and the well-balanced face states |
| @sec-ch06 | Where the work of gravity is booked, what each form conserves, and the gravity work inside the vertical implicit correction |
| @sec-ch07 | Every source term besides the flux divergence and gravity: the forcing loop, axial angular momentum, Coriolis, viscosity and heat conduction, heating, relaxation, sponges and user stage forcings |
| @sec-ch08 | The moist side of a stage and what keeps the state admissible: saturation adjustment, sedimentation, the flux positivity limiter, the equation-of-state floors, their records and the redo decision |
| @sec-ch09 | Advancing in time: the Runge–Kutta stages, the time-step bound, step acceptance and redo, and the implicit column solve |
| @sec-ch10 | The flux register every face flux goes through: its posts, the prescribed faces, the wall batch, the step amounts, the monitor counts, the rollback of a rejected step, and the conservation budget read from it |
| @sec-ch11 | The boundary conditions, the ghost fill and exchange order, and immersed solids |
| @sec-ch12 | Build options, environment switches, YAML scheme selection and which switch combinations are tested |
| @sec-ch13 | The conservation budgets and diagnostics the model prints, and the tests that read them |
| @sec-ch14 | Several processes and devices, output and restart files, and reproducibility |
| @sec-ch15 | How deck keys become options, how output is written and combined, and how a run is restarted |
| @sec-ch16 | How the code is verified: the bitwise gates, the capture sweep, launch counting, regression provenance and device reproducibility, then the verification catalogue: which test supports which claim, and how to rerun it |
| @sec-ch17 | The limits of every chapter in one place: where snapy can be wrong, restricted or awkward |

The appendices are reference tables: notation (@sec-appa), the derivation index (@sec-appb), the test index
(@sec-appc), the environment switches (@sec-appd), the external components (@sec-appe), a topic index, the V3 lane
map and task map (@sec-appg), the glossary (@sec-apph), the deck keys (@sec-appi) and the source tree (@sec-appj).

## Pins {.unnumbered}

Code is cited by file and symbol, resolved at one pinned commit of
[`chengcli/snapy`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy). That commit is recorded in `doc/tech-report/code_pin.yml`
and printed in the build note below for readers of the PDF. Every code citation identifies a file and, where applicable, a symbol at that pinned commit.

## Install and run {#sec-preface-install .unnumbered}

Every input file, switch and command in this book is written for snapy at the pin above, built from source. The
releases on PyPI (`pip install snapy`) are older than the pin. They lack the environment switches of chapters 4 to
6 (`SNAP_WB_REF4`, `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE`, `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`), and a
switch the code does not know is ignored without a message. Older releases also refuse the `gravity-work` keys of
chapter 6. So build the pin, as below, before you try any example.

<!-- generated reader-reference: install -->
**What you need.** Python `>=3.10` ([`pyproject.toml:25`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/pyproject.toml#L25)), CMake 3.22 or later (`cmake_minimum_required`, [`CMakeLists.txt:1`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/CMakeLists.txt#L1)), a C++17 compiler (`CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD`, [`CMakeLists.txt:3`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/CMakeLists.txt#L3)), and the NetCDF C library. Install the latter with `brew install netcdf` on macOS or `sudo apt install libnetcdf-dev` on Debian/Ubuntu.

**Build the source pin.** The Python dependencies below follow [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/pyproject.toml); the CMake options explicitly enable the example drivers and disable the optional UCX and parallel-NetCDF backends for this single-machine build.

```bash
python3 -m venv snapy-env && source snapy-env/bin/activate
pip install numpy pyyaml "kintera>=2.6.13" torch==2.10.0
git clone https://github.com/chengcli/snapy && cd snapy
git checkout 73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=OFF -DUCX=OFF
cmake --build build --parallel 6
pip install .
```
<!-- end reader-reference: install -->

`-DUCX=OFF` builds the Gloo backend only, which is all a single machine needs; @sec-ch14-backends describes UCX.
The build also compiles the tests (`BUILD_TESTS` is on by default). A test named in a Tests layer runs with
`ctest --test-dir build -R <name>`; to reproduce a documented test case and check it against the book, follow
@sec-ch16-metrics. The last line installs the Python package from the same build, which the Python
listings of the chapters import (`import snapy`). It puts `pd-combine` and `pd-inspect` on the path as entry points
(`pd-combine`, [`pyproject.toml:54`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/pyproject.toml#L54); `pd-inspect`, [`pyproject.toml:55`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/pyproject.toml#L55)) and installs
the `api/pd-run` script beside them (`script-files`, [`pyproject.toml:61`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/pyproject.toml#L61)).

**Run a deck.** The build puts one driver program per example in `build/bin`, next to links to the decks of
`examples/`. A deck is a YAML input file, and a *driver* is the program that reads it, sets the initial state
and steps the model ({{< code examples/straka.cpp ParseArguments >}},
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). See @sec-ch01-initialization
for the distinction between a deck, a case and a restart file. The Straka cold bubble runs on one process with

```bash
cd build/bin
./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

It prints one line per ten cycles and stops at 900 s of model time, after about 3700 cycles (half a minute on six
CPU cores). It writes `straka_single.out0.00000.nc` and `straka_single.out0.00001.nc`, the start and the end state.
A deck split into several blocks runs on several processes, launched with `torchrun`. The number of processes $N$
is the number of blocks divided by `blocks_per_process`. `straka_proc2.yaml` has two blocks along $x_2$ and one
block per process, so $N = 2$ (about 20 s):

```bash
torchrun --no-python --nproc-per-node=2 --master-port=29573 ./straka.release straka_proc2.yaml
```

Pick any free port for `--master-port` (@sec-ch14-launch). A process count that does not match the deck stops at
construction with "world_size (1) does not match layout partitioning (2)".

The 2-D warm-bubble test is `bryan.yaml`, a moist warm bubble on one block ($x_1$ by $x_2$, 200 by 400 cells): its
`problem` card sets the bubble's amplitude `dT`, centre `xc`, `zc` and radii `xr`, `zr`. It runs the same way,
`./bryan.release bryan.yaml`, stops at 1000 s of model time and writes one output frame every 100 s.

**The same example on one GPU.** Rebuild with the `CUDA` option on
([`CMakeLists.txt:10`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/CMakeLists.txt#L10)),
that is, with `-DCUDA=ON` added to the build command above, then select the device with two environment variables:

```bash
cd build/bin
DEVICE=cuda DEVICE_ID=0 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

`DEVICE` defaults to `cpu`
([`src/layout/layout.cpp:288`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/layout/layout.cpp#L288));
with `cuda`, the block runs on `cuda:<DEVICE_ID>`, or on the local rank's GPU when `DEVICE_ID` is unset
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::device_str >}}).
The driver prints "Running on CUDA" before the first step when it got a GPU
(`main` of {{< code examples/straka.cpp main >}});
without that line it is running on the CPU. @sec-ch14-gpu covers the rest of GPU execution.

**Which driver for which deck.** `straka.release` runs dry Cartesian decks such as `straka_single.yaml`;
`bryan.release` runs the moist `bryan.yaml`; `run_hydro.release -i <deck>` needs a deck with a `reactions:` card,
such as `jupiter_evap_precip_1d.yaml`, and stops on a dry deck. A "minimal input" in a chapter is a fragment, not
a deck: add its keys to a copy of a complete deck (`straka_single.yaml` for a dry run, `bryan.yaml` for a moist
one) and run that copy. An environment switch goes in front of the driver, as in
`SNAP_WB_REF4=1 ./straka.release deck.yaml`.
